activity:7508036462769188865.title:
One Comet  ad lived for 33 days. Another lasted just 1.

Same brand. Same studio. Same shoe.
So what changed?

We decoded all 42 Comet ads currently live on Meta to understand what they were testing, what they kept repeating, and what actually stayed in market.

The data tells a pretty interesting story.
Most of Comet’s ads follow a very consistent creative formula:
• 100% sell the look, not the shoe
• 88% go straight to the product
• 83% use clean studio shoots
• 67% open with the shoe immediately
• 95% show no proof
• 86% have no clear purchase CTA

But here’s where it gets interesting.
The plainest ads were the ones that stayed live the longest.

And the ads that tried to be funny or surprising were switched off faster.
Why?
It wasn’t because the audience didn’t want entertainment.

It was because the longer-running ads were more specific about who they were speaking to.

Streetwear. Minimalist.
Not “anyone with taste.”

Swipe through the carousel to see:
• What Comet is repeating
• What its longest-running ads have in common
• What gets switched off faster
• And the creative gap hiding in plain sight

This is the kind of competitive intelligence we’re building at Galvor.ai
